section_1.title: Prerequisite & The 2D 'Pseudo-Scalar'
section_1.content: Briefly review vectors. Explain that in 2D, the 'cross product' is actually a signed area of a parallelogram. It represents how much two vectors are 'perpendicular' to each other, resulting in a scalar (magnitude only) indicating rotation direction (clockwise vs. counter-clockwise).
section_1.example: Visualize a robotic arm in 2D: The cross product of the arm vector and the force vector determines if the arm rotates clockwise or counter-clockwise.

section_2.title: The 3D Definition: Creating Space
section_2.content: Transition to 3D: The cross product is a vector perpendicular to the plane formed by the two input vectors. Introduce the Right-Hand Rule (RHR) visually: Point fingers along vector A, curl to B, thumb points in the direction of the new vector C.
section_2.example: Imagine a chameleon on a 3D grid: If its tongue extends along vector A and its tail aligns with vector B, the cross product vector shows the precise direction the chameleon must jump to stay perfectly balanced perpendicular to both.

section_3.title: The Algebraic Formula (The Determinant)
section_3.content: Present the determinant formula using i, j, k basis vectors. Explain that this mechanical method calculates the components (x, y, z) of the resulting vector. Keep the visual clean: a 3x3 matrix layout that reveals the cross-multiplication pattern.
section_3.example: Calculate the cross product for vectors A=(1, 2, 3) and B=(4, 5, 6) step-by-step using the matrix expansion method.

section_4.title: Geometric Meaning & Real-World Application
section_4.content: Reinforce that the magnitude |A x B| = |A||B|sin(θ), representing the area of a 3D parallelogram. Conclude with a physics application: Torque. Torque = r x F, showing why applying force at 90 degrees yields the most rotation.
section_4.example: A wrench tightening a bolt: The cross product of the wrench's length (r) and the hand's force (F) produces a torque vector pointing along the bolt's axis, causing it to move forward.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite & The 2D 'Pseudo-Scalar'", [
            "2D cross product measures signed parallelogram area.",
            "It indicates rotation direction: clockwise or counter-clockwise.",
            "It represents the perpendicularity of two vectors."
        ])
        
        # Setup Coordinate Plane and Vectors
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 4], y_range=[-2, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6")
        
        u = Vector([2, 1], color="#FF6666")
        v = Vector([1, 2], color="#66CCFF")
        
        # Position them relative to origin
        u.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - u.get_start())
        v.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - v.get_start())
        
        u_label = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color="#FF6666").next_to(u.get_end(), RIGHT)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#66CCFF").next_to(v.get_end(), UP)
        
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            axes.c2p(2, 1),
            axes.c2p(3, 3),
            axes.c2p(1, 2),
            color="#FFFF66",
            fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\text{Area} = |u_1v_2 - u_2v_1|", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(u), Write(u_label), Create(v), Write(v_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF66")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF66")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF66")
        
        self.wait(2)
